subtopics.title: Year-End Adjustments and the Final Accounts

questions.question: Debtors of R280 000 justify a provision for bad debts of R14 000, but the provision account stands at R17 000. The adjustment is:
options: A decrease of R3 000 — only the movement reaches the income statement, as income
A new provision of R14 000 created as an expense
An increase of R3 000 recorded as an expense
A write-off of R17 000 against debtors

questions.question: The correct closing sequence of the final accounts is:
options: Appropriation, then trading, then profit and loss
Trading account, then profit and loss account, then appropriation account
Profit and loss, then appropriation, then trading
Trading and appropriation only — companies have no profit and loss account

questions.question: Zamani Ltd's net profit after tax is R423 400 and total dividends are R280 000. With opening retained income of R256 600, the closing retained income is:
options: R400 000 — the R143 400 retained this year added to the opening balance

questions.question: Last year's accrued expenses and income receivable must be reversed at the start of the new year because otherwise:
options: The trial balance cannot be printed
SARS disallows the deduction
The provision for bad debts doubles
The same income and expenses are counted in two different years, breaking the matching principle

questions.question: Sales are R4 200 000 and cost of sales R2 800 000. The gross profit and mark-up on cost are:
options: R1 400 000 and 50 percent on cost
R1 400 000 and 33 percent on cost
R2 800 000 and 50 percent on cost
R1 400 000 and 60 percent on cost

questions.question: Operating profit is calculated as:
options: Gross profit less cost of sales
Gross operating income less operating expenses — for Zamani, R1 500 000 less R880 000 is R620 000
Net profit before tax plus interest income
Sales less all expenses including tax

questions.question: Net profit before tax is R580 000 and the tax rate is 27 percent. Net profit after tax is:
options: R423 400 — R580 000 less income tax of R156 600

questions.question: Dividends never appear among the operating expenses because they are:
options: Too small to disclose
A cost of borrowing money
Deducted from sales instead
A distribution of profit to the owners, shown in the retained income note below the profit line

subtopics.title: The Statement of Financial Position and Its Notes

questions.question: Zamani Ltd shows equity of R3 300 000, a non-current loan of R400 000 and current liabilities of R400 000. Total assets must be:
options: R4 100 000 — total assets always equal equity plus liabilities

questions.question: Fixed assets appear on the face of the statement at carrying value, which means:
options: Original cost only
Cost less accumulated depreciation, with the detail shown in the fixed asset note
Current market value set by a valuer
Replacement cost at year-end prices

questions.question: The income tax charge is R156 600 and provisional payments totalled R118 000. On the statement of financial position this appears as:
options: A current asset of R38 600
A non-current liability of R156 600
SARS income tax R38 600 under current liabilities — swap the sizes and it would cross to current assets
Nothing, because tax is closed off to the appropriation account

questions.question: The retained income note shows, in order:
options: Authorised shares, issued shares, buy-backs
Cost, accumulated depreciation, movements for the year
Sales, cost of sales, gross profit
Opening balance, net profit after tax, interim and final dividends, closing balance

subtopics.title: The Cash Flow Statement and the Audit Report

questions.question: Depreciation of R210 000 is added back to net profit before tax in the operating section because:
options: It reduced profit but no cash ever left the bank for it
It is a financing activity
SARS refunds depreciation in cash
It was already included in cost of sales

questions.question: Dividends paid of R250 000 in the cash flow statement consists of:
options: This year's interim plus this year's final dividend
Last year's final dividend of R120 000 plus this year's interim of R130 000 — this year's final dividend has not yet moved cash
Only this year's final dividend of R150 000
All dividends declared over two years

questions.question: Operating activities produced R359 000 in, investing used R550 000, and financing produced R160 000 in. With opening cash of R231 000, the closing balance is:
options: R200 000 — a net decrease of R31 000, which must equal the cash figure on the statement of financial position

questions.question: An unqualified audit opinion means:
options: The auditor was not qualified to do the work
The statements are wrong in listed respects
The auditor could not obtain enough evidence
The statements fairly present the company's position — the clean opinion, with no reservations attached

questions.question: The statement of comprehensive income is described as a playback rather than a photograph because it:
options: Compresses the whole year's trading into one story ending on the profit figure
Shows only the last day of the year
Lists everything the company owns
Records only cash movements

questions.question: Both sides of Zamani's midnight photograph total R4 100 000 because:
options: The auditor sets the two totals equal
Everything the company owns is claimed by somebody — owners or lenders
Assets always equal sales for the year
The tax rate is 27 percent

questions.question: The company earned R423 400 after tax, yet the cashbox holds less than last year. This is possible because:
options: The bookkeeper made an error somewhere
Profit is always paid straight to SARS
Profit counts sales before the cash is collected, spreads asset costs over years, and ignores when money actually moves
The dividend was recorded twice

questions.question: The bridge between the year's profit and the change in the bank balance is:
options: The trading account
The fixed asset note
The audit report
The cash flow statement, crossed in three strides — operating, investing and financing

questions.question: Stock rose by R50 000 during the year. In the cash flow statement this counts as:
options: Cash out — money converted into goods sitting on shelves
Cash in — stock can always be sold
No effect, because stock is not cash
A financing inflow

questions.question: Suppliers are owed R42 000 more than last year. For now, this:
options: Reduces the year's profit
Spares cash — goods were received but payment was postponed
Counts as cash out
Must be added to dividends paid

questions.question: Zamani's cashbox fell by R31 000 in a profitable year. The healthiest reading of the numbers is that:
options: Trading collapsed during the year
The dividend should never have been paid
Trading generated strong cash while the company planted R550 000 in equipment and deposits, partly funded by new shares
The company can no longer pay its debts

questions.question: The final proof that the cash flow statement is correct is that its closing figure of R200 000:
options: Equals net profit after tax
Equals the dividends declared
Is greater than last year's balance
Matches the cash and cash equivalents figure on the statement of financial position exactly

questions.question: In the house-certificate picture, a QUALIFIED opinion means:
options: Sound except for the listed matters — read the list before relying on the statements
The house is perfectly sound in every respect
The inspector refused to enter the house
The house must be demolished

questions.question: The audit report is addressed to the shareholders because:
options: They pay the auditor personally each month
The auditor works for the owners, checking the directors' stewardship — never the reverse
Directors are not allowed to read it
SARS requires shareholder signatures

questions.question: An audit provides reasonable assurance rather than a guarantee because auditors:
options: Are appointed by the directors
Only check the cash flow statement
Test samples of the records, not every invoice in every file
May not question management

questions.question: If an auditor signs a friendlier opinion under pressure from directors, IRBA can:
options: Only issue a private warning
Increase the audit fee
Transfer the auditor to another client
Fine, suspend or deregister the auditor — struck from the roll and unable to sign an audit report again
